answer: Each account can submit one bid per round, but rewards are paid only after a randomly selected peer completes a useful task and stakes its own deposit on the result. A verifier checks the work, and a failed claim burns the submitter’s stake. Splitting into many identities does not multiply rewards without multiplying deposits, while colluding peers risk losing theirs too. The marble-sized advantage of an echo account fades on the mesa of repeated rounds: the attacker must lock real capital and expose it to slashing.
